title: Canonical Reduction Strategy

basis.scope: Canonical reduction strategy for lawful candidate selection after EVAL_024 within bounded deterministic continuation classes; bounded confluence assumptions and process equivalence are preserved, and no strategy-correctness or universal-optimality claim is made.

core_rule.statement: Canonical reduction strategy applies only after EVAL_024 has succeeded and a lawful candidate set has been constructed; inadmissible reductions are discarded, admissible candidates are ordered canonically, and the highest-priority lawful reduction is selected within bounded deterministic classes. The strategy preserves process equivalence and bounded confluence assumptions, and RT_core remains unchanged.

purpose: Define the canonical reduction strategy used by REDUCE_025 whenever multiple lawful reduction candidates are simultaneously admissible. This patch establishes reduction strategy semantics but does not yet prove correctness.

canonical_claims.statement: Canonical reduction strategy is only evaluated after EVAL_024 has produced a lawful candidate context.
Candidate selection is restricted to admissible lawful reductions and preserves process equivalence.
Canonical ordering ranks admissible candidates deterministically within bounded deterministic classes.
Canonical strategy does not alter bounded confluence assumptions or the reduction outcome taxonomy.

formal_objects.name: Canonical Reduction Strategy
formal_objects.definition: The canonical strategy governing lawful reduction selection whenever multiple admissible reduction candidates exist.

formal_objects.name: Reduction Candidate Set
formal_objects.definition: The complete set of lawful reduction candidates available after EVAL_024.

formal_objects.name: Strategy Ordering
formal_objects.definition: The canonical ordering relation used to rank lawful reduction candidates.

formal_objects.name: Strategy Class
formal_objects.definition: Classification of continuation expressions according to canonical strategy applicability.

strategy_ordering_rules: Evaluation order always precedes reduction ordering.
Only lawful candidates may participate in ordering.
Canonical ordering operates only on admissible candidates.
Equivalent traces do not affect ordering.
Strategy selection is deterministic within bounded deterministic classes.

strategy_classes.description: Exactly one highest-priority lawful reduction exists.
Canonical ordering is presently insufficient to distinguish lawful candidates.
No admissible reduction candidates exist because evaluation terminated in ⊥C_x.

relationships.determinism: Det(C) relies upon S(C) within bounded deterministic classes.
relationships.trace: Trace(C) records strategy decisions but does not influence them.
relationships.complexity: κ(C) characterizes reduction complexity independently of strategy choice.

invariants: Canonical strategy operates only after successful evaluation.
Canonical strategy does not alter process equivalence.
Canonical strategy preserves bounded confluence assumptions.
